{"notes": "Visit 2 (left 2:30). Board: one connected chain from the start runs along the belly and reaches the tail, ending in a curl at about x=25-28. Some dominoes bunch tightly near x=25, y=9, which looks like a crowded or awkward fork join. The back/top line from the nose (pale, ~x4-11, y9 to 6) is NOT connected to the start; there's a visible gap at the nose. It is the key open risk with about 7.5 min left. I can't tell who placed which dominoes, so I'm judging only on what I saw and heard.

Hana: Said she's on the lower tail fork and wants a dry run and a join check once the top and belly lines are across. Good process thinking and sensible sequencing, and she's still setting direction. Her claim that the lower fork will 'lay itself' once the belly arrives is a bit optimistic, since the belly has arrived and the tail join looks cramped. Check that she follows through.

Omar: Now speaking up and has a clear task (upper tail fork, stroke 3), announced to the team. Good that he's contributing and communicating. Concern: the top line isn't across yet, so the upper fork may be getting built before its feed line exists. Verify what he does next.

Jack: Nothing new seen. Owns the sketch and layout. Check whether the back line gets connected to the nose, since he was the bottleneck earlier.

Sofia: Nothing new seen. She was to trace the belly line, and a belly line now exists, but I can't confirm who built it. Ask her directly and watch the back line.

Next visit: check that the back line is connected at the nose, whether the dry run happens, and the tail fork join quality."}
